LESSON: CHILDREN’S OBLIGATIONS TO OTHER FAMILY MEMBERS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Muamalaat
Topic 6.3: Children’s Obligations to Other Family Members
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Children’s Obligations to Other Family Members, part of Muamalaat in Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: How do you develop good relationship with other family members? 3. What is the significance of strengthening your relationship with other family members?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. prepare chart with names of extended family members and hang strategically,

2. discuss children’s obligations to other family members (such as respect, visiting, attending ceremonies, helping and caring for them), in pairs/groups, and write the point in their notebook,

3. brainstorm the significance of fulfilling obligations to other family members,

4. dramatise their obligations to other family members. 1. Who are the other family members? 2.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. prepare chart with names of extended family members and hang strategically,
2. discuss children’s obligations to other family members (such as respect, visiting, attending ceremonies, helping and caring for them), in pairs/groups, and write the point in their notebook,
3. brainstorm the significance of fulfilling obligations to other family members,
4. dramatise their obligations to other family members. 1. Who are the other family members? 2.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Children’s Obligations to Other Family Members together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: the skill of listening, speaking and writing enhanced as learners discuss children’s

obligations to other family members (e.g. respect, visiting, attending ceremonies, helping and caring for them), in

pairs/groups, and write the points in their notebook

• Critical thinking and problem solving: the skill of evaluation and decision making is enhanced as learners discuss the

significance of fulfilling obligations to other family members, in pairs/groups.

39

• Creativity and imagination: the skill of networking enhanced as learners dramatise their obligations to other family members.

• Learn to learn: the skill of sharing learnt knowledge enhanced as learners prepare chart with names of extended family

members and hang strategically.

Values:
• Respect: acceptance enhanced as learners respect each other’s opinions while discussing, in groups.

• Responsibility: accountability as learners prepare chart with names of extended family members and hang strategically.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion as learners relate well with family and other members of the society.

Link to other learning areas:

Social Studies as learners fulfil their duties towards family and other members of the society.
